summary: Large malformed chunked multipart upload triggers proxy buffer growth and upstream runtime OOMs causing elevated 5xx rates
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 03:20 UTC we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses for a single enterprise tenant (AcmeRetail) routed through the us-east-1 API-Gateway cluster. The traffic pattern correlated with a spike of large multipart/chunked uploads from that tenant. The API gateway proxy started allocating large per-connection buffers while parsing malformed chunk metadata; this drove memory pressure on the ingress proxies and led to upstream runtime processes (serving-runtime) OOMing and restarting. Impact: ~18% 5xx rate for the tenant across multiple routes, intermittent streaming disconnects, and several customer-facing requests failing for ~40 minutes during the peak. This is customer-impacting and blocking their QPS-critical ingest flows.
impact: Customer-facing elevated 5xx across text generation and streaming endpoints for AcmeRetail. Observed increased retry storms from client (hedged retries), and temporary rate loss for 2 internal services depending on tenant-specific routing. Estimated ~1500 failed requests during event window.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) From a client in us-east-1, send a POST to /v1/streams with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and intentionally malformed chunk sizes (e.g., send an undersized chunk length header followed by larger payload).
2) Attach a large file part (~30–200MB) in a single chunk frame while keeping connection open.
3) Repeat at ~5 concurrent connections to reproduce buffer growth quickly.
4) Observe api-gateway proxy memory climb and serving-runtime OOM logs in ~30–90s.

[2026-03-10T03:21:06Z] apigw-proxy-12: allocating buffer 32768 -> 104857600 for connection tenant=acme-retail
[2026-03-10T03:21:22Z] ingress-proxy-7: memory pressure high: rss 92%
[2026-03-10T03:21:28Z] serving-runtime-3: runtime OOM: failed alloc 104857600
[2026-03-10T03:21:30Z] serving-runtime-3: watchdog restart triggered (exit code=137)
[2026-03-10T03:22:10Z] apigw-metrics: 5xx_rate tenant=acme-retail window=5m value=0.18
[2026-03-10T03:58:01Z] apigw-alert: resolved: proxy memory normalized
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis considered DNS/timeouts or backpressure amplification. After correlating access logs and buffer metrics, the pattern pointed at malformed chunked bodies causing the http parser to fallback to a slow-path that accumulates data in memory until either a full delimiter or timeout. The parser does not enforce a strict per-request content-length cap for Transfer-Encoding: chunked, so large or malformed chunks can cause the proxy to allocate progressively larger buffers. The ingress-proxy runs in the same node pool as serving-runtime processes; when the proxy RSS climbed, kernel OOM killer targeted runtime processes rather than the proxy (smaller oom_score_adj), causing upstream restarts and 502/503s. Heap snapshots from a warmed serving-runtime instance show large slab allocations immediately before OOM.
mitigation:
1) Immediate: added an ingress rule to throttle and reject chunked uploads > 16MB for the AcmeRetail tenant via per-tenant rate-limit policy (applied at 03:30 UTC).
2) Rolling restart of ingress-proxy pool with tightened ulimit and earlier buffer reclaim behavior applied (03:45 UTC).
3) Customer advised to stop large multipart uploads and switch to signed pre-signed object uploads to S3 for large files; support provided sample client code (03:50 UTC).
resolution: Partial mitigation applied and service returned to normative 5xx levels by 04:10 UTC after ingress throttles and restart. Permanent remediation tracked in follow-up tasks: tighten the parser limits, ensure proxies are preferable OOM targets, and add per-connection chunk size cap. No long-term data loss detected. Incident remains open pending code fix rollout.
root_cause: Ingress HTTP parser allowed malformed chunk metadata to drive unbounded per-connection buffer growth under Transfer-Encoding: chunked. The ingress proxy and serving runtime co-location led to memory pressure killing upstream runtime processes, producing elevated 5xx.
workaround: Apply tenant-scoped content-size and chunked-upload rejection rules. Recommend customers upload large blobs via object-storage workflows instead of embedding large multipart uploads through the API gateway.
next_steps:
- SRE/Runtime: implement a hard cap on per-connection buffered bytes for chunked transfer (PR proposed: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521) - Target: 2026-03-17.
- Gateway: add parsing defensive checks and early 4xx on malformed chunk headers. Target: 2026-03-16.
- Ops: move ingress proxy to dedicated nodes (isolate from serving-runtime) as a medium-term deployment change. Target: 2026-04-01.
- Product/Solutions: document recommended large-file ingestion patterns for enterprise tenants. Target: 2026-03-20.
